newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BT in bid to remove RPT manager.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BT in bid to remove RPT manager.

text.p: Bankers Trust International (BT), which holds a 19.6 percent stake in Rural Property Trust (RPT), said on Monday it had requisitioned an extraordinary meeting to remove the manager of RPT, Rural and Agricultural Management (RAM).

"BT is concerned that under RAM management, the Trust has consistently underperformed, has traded significantly below its net tangible asset backing and has demonstrated a poor track record of profitability," BT International Managing Director Lawrence Hudson said in a statement.

"We consider that management has failed to implement promised changes to its asset portfolio and corporate structure and we are very dissatisfied with the lack of progress on both counts," Hudson said.
RPT must convene a meeting of unitholders within 21 days of the serving of a requisition.
BT said RAM's track record showed it had it would not perform up to the levels expected by unit holders.

BT pointed to an aggregate net operating loss since June 30, 1991, RPT's unit price consistently trading at a discount to net tangible asset of more than 20 percent and no dividend payments since listing in 1994.
RPT closed down two cents at 42 cents on Friday and was untraded at 11.10 a.m. (0010 GMT). RPT's net asset backing at December 31 was 55.11 cents.
RPT reported a A$2.35 million profit for the six months to December 31 1996 last month, compared with a A$2.81 million loss in the same half a year earlier.
BT said any new manager would have a commitment to review the corporate structure and the corporate governance policies of the trust.
BT said it would put forward a qualified and experienced candidate for the manager's role and did not seek the role itself.
BT's Hudson later told Reuters he had advised the other major shareholders of the plan to remove RAM as RPT's manager.
He said BT had been actively trying to improve RAM's performance in the last year, but had now decided their removal was necessary.
"It's been quite a struggle and I don't enjoy the active role I've found myself having to assume here, but I don't think that the current manager is going to improve the performance," Hudson said.
He said he would not be impressed if RAM said the poor performance was due to a depressed Australian regional ecomomy since the drought of the early 1990s.
BT had bought its stake in two tranches in late 1995 and mid 1996 at an average cost of 47 cents per unit.
RAM was not immediately available for comment.
